newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICAN DAILY PORT, SHIPPING UPDATE FOR AUG 6.
newsitem.headline: MEXICAN DAILY PORT, SHIPPING UPDATE FOR AUG 6.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open to shipping on Wednesday as Hurricane Guillermo continued to float to sea, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.

Guillermo was reported moving further from Mexico's Baja California state coast to 961 miles (1538 km) west of the Pacific's Socorro island. The ministry warned ships from sailing in the vicinity of the hurricane.
The ministry said the storm would not affect the country, and was continuing to distance itself from the coast.

Smaller vessels were warned against sailing along the coast of Baja California, Sinaloa and Nayarit states because of strong winds. Strong gusts also in the Gulf of Tehuantepec of up to 20 knots (22 miles/38 km per hour) and waves up to eight feet high.
Isolated storms and wind gusts in the northeastern gulf. Along rest of coast sunny skies and waves three to six feet high.
